At the time opinion held that the Wei prefecture army was still intact, the Khitan would fear Shandong, would not dare go south, and the imperial carriage could visit Yecheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the Emperor heard that Jin'an camp had fallen to the enemy. An edict ordered removal to Heyang. At the time opinion held that the Wei prefecture army was still intact, the Khitan would fear Shandong and would not dare go south, and the imperial carriage could visit Yecheng.

sentences.zh: 帝以李崧與範延光相善，召入謀之。

translations.literal: Because Li Song was on good terms with Fan Yanguang, the Emperor summoned him to consult.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Song was on good terms with Fan Yanguang, the Emperor summoned him to consult.

sentences.zh: 薛文遇不知而繼至，帝變色，崧躡文遇足，乃出。

translations.literal: Xue Wenyü, not knowing, arrived next; the Emperor's expression changed; Song trod on Wenyü's foot, and then left.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wenyü, not knowing, arrived next. The Emperor's expression changed. Song trod on Wenyü's foot, and then left.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我見此物肉顫，適擬抽刀刺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "When I see this creature my flesh trembles; I was just about to draw my knife and stab him."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "When I see this creature my flesh trembles. I was just about to draw my knife and stab him."

sentences.zh: 」崧曰：「文遇小人，致誤大事，刺之益醜。

translations.literal: " Song said: "Wenyü is a petty man who caused great affairs to go wrong; stabbing him would only make the ugliness worse."
translations.idiomatic: " Song said: "Wenyü is a petty man who ruined great affairs. Stabbing him would only make the ugliness worse."

sentences.zh: 」崧因請帝歸京。

translations.literal: " Song then asked the Emperor to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " Song then urged the Emperor to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 壬申，車駕至河陽。

translations.literal: On renshen, the imperial carriage reached Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the imperial carriage reached Heyang.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，晉高祖與契丹至潞州，契丹遣蕃將大相溫率五千騎送晉高祖南行。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the Jin Founder and the Khitan reached Luzhou; the Khitan sent the barbarian general Daxiangwen with five thousand horsemen to escort the Jin Founder south.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the Jin Founder and the Khitan reached Luzhou. The Khitan sent the barbarian general Daxiangwen with five thousand horsemen to escort the Jin Founder south.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，車駕至自河陽。

translations.literal: On dingchou, the imperial carriage arrived from Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the imperial carriage arrived from Heyang.

sentences.zh: 時左右勸帝固守河陽。

translations.literal: At the time those around him urged the Emperor to hold firm at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time those around him urged the Emperor to hold firm at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 居數日，符彥饒、張彥琪至，奏帝不可城守。

translations.literal: After several days, Fu Yanrao and Zhang Yanqi arrived and memorialized that the Emperor could not defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: After several days Fu Yanrao and Zhang Yanqi arrived and reported that the Emperor could not defend the city.

sentences.zh: 是日晚，至東上門，小黃門鳴鞘於路，索然無聲。

translations.literal: That evening he reached the Upper East Gate; the junior palace attendants struck their scabbards along the road, yet all was desolately silent.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he reached the Upper East Gate. The junior palace attendants struck their scabbards along the road, yet all was desolately silent.

sentences.zh: 己卯，帝遣馬軍都指揮使宋審虔率千餘騎至白馬坡，言踏陣地，時諸將謂審虔曰：「何地不堪交戰，誰人肯立於此？

translations.literal: On jimao, the Emperor dispatched Song Shenqian, commander of the cavalry, with more than a thousand horsemen to White Horse Slope, saying it was ground to tread the battle line; at the time the generals said to Shenqian: "What ground is not fit for battle? Who would be willing to stand here?"
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the Emperor dispatched Song Shenqian, commander of the cavalry, with more than a thousand horsemen to White Horse Slope, saying it was ground on which to take the battle line. At the time the generals said to Shenqian: "What ground is not fit for battle? Who would be willing to stand here?"

sentences.zh: 」審虔乃請帝還宮。

translations.literal: " Shenqian then asked the Emperor to return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Shenqian then asked the Emperor to return to the palace.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，晉高祖至河陽。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Jin Founder reached Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the Jin Founder reached Heyang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳辰時，帝舉族與皇太后曹氏自燔於元武樓。

translations.literal: On xinsi at the chen hour, the Emperor, his entire clan, and Empress Dowager Cao burned themselves at the Yuanwu Tower.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi at the chen hour the Emperor, his entire clan, and Empress Dowager Cao burned themselves at the Yuanwu Tower.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖入洛，得帝燼骨於火中，來年三月，詔葬於徽陵之封中。

translations.literal: The Jin Founder entered Luoyang, obtained the Emperor's charred bones from the fire, and in the third month of the following year ordered burial within the mound of Hui Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Founder entered Luoyang, recovered the Emperor's charred bones from the fire, and in the third month of the following year ordered burial within the mound of Hui Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝在位共二年，年五十二。

translations.literal: The Emperor reigned in all two years and was fifty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had reigned for two years in all and was fifty-two years old.

sentences.zh: （《五代史闕文》：晉高祖引契丹圍晉安寨，降楊光遠。

translations.literal: (The 《Supplementary Texts to the History of the Five Dynasties》: the Jin Founder led the Khitan to besiege Jin'an camp and received Yang Guangyuan's surrender.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Supplementary Texts to the History of the Five Dynasties》 records that the Jin Founder led the Khitan to besiege Jin'an camp and received Yang Guangyuan's surrender.

sentences.zh: 清泰帝至自覃懷，京師父老迎帝於上東門外，帝垂泣不止。

translations.literal: The Qingtai Emperor arrived from Tanhuai; the elders of the capital welcomed the Emperor outside the Upper East Gate; the Emperor wept without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The Qingtai Emperor arrived from Tanhuai. The elders of the capital welcomed him outside the Upper East Gate, and the Emperor wept without cease.

sentences.zh: 父老奏曰：「臣等伏聞前唐時中國有難，帝王多幸蜀以圖進取。

translations.literal: The elders memorialized: "Your subjects have heard that in former Tang times when China was in difficulty, emperors often visited Shu to plan recovery.
translations.idiomatic: The elders said: "We have heard that in former Tang times when China was in difficulty, emperors often went to Shu to plan recovery.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不且入西川？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, why not for the time being enter Western Chuan?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, why not for the time being go to Western Chuan?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「本朝兩川節度使皆用文臣，所以玄宗、僖宗避寇幸蜀。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "In our dynasty the military governors of the two Chuan circuits have all been civil officials; that is why Emperor Xuanzong and Emperor Xizong, fleeing bandits, were able to visit Shu.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said: "In our dynasty the military governors of the two Chuan circuits have all been civil officials. That is why Emperor Xuanzong and Emperor Xizong, fleeing bandits, were able to go to Shu.

sentences.zh: 今孟氏已稱尊矣，吾何歸乎！

translations.literal: Now the Meng clan has already proclaimed itself sovereign—where could I return!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the Meng clan has already proclaimed itself sovereign. Where could I go!"

sentences.zh: 」因慟哭入內，舉族自焚。）〉

translations.literal: " He then wailed and entered within; his entire clan burned themselves.)]
translations.idiomatic: " He then wailed and went inside. His entire clan burned themselves.)]

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：末帝負神武之才，有人君之量。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Last Emperor possessed divine martial talent and the measure of a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: The Last Emperor possessed divine martial talent and the measure of a true ruler.

sentences.zh: 由尋戈而踐阼，慚德應深；

translations.literal: having seized the throne by seeking the halberd, his shame in virtue should have been deep;
translations.idiomatic: Having seized the throne by force, his shame in virtue should have been deep;

sentences.zh: 及當寧以居尊，政經未失。

translations.literal: yet when he took the throne and dwelt in honor, he did not lose the threads of government.
translations.idiomatic: yet once he took the throne and dwelt in honor, he did not lose the threads of government.

sentences.zh: 屬天命不祐，人謀匪臧，坐俟焚如，良可悲矣！

translations.literal: It happened that Heaven's mandate did not protect him and human plans were not good; he sat and awaited being burned—truly pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: But Heaven's mandate did not protect him and human counsel was not sound. He sat and awaited the flames. Truly pitiable!

sentences.zh: 稽夫衽金甲於河壖之際，斧眺樓於梁壘之時，出沒如神，何其勇也！

translations.literal: Consider how when he spread golden armor on the river bank and gazed from the tower with axe at the Liang ramparts, he appeared and vanished like a spirit—how brave he was!
translations.idiomatic: Consider how when he spread golden armor on the river bank and gazed from the tower with axe at the Liang ramparts, he appeared and vanished like a spirit. How brave he was!

sentences.zh: 及乎駐革輅於覃懷之日，絕羽書於汾晉之辰，涕淚沾襟，何其怯也！

translations.literal: Yet when he halted his leather carriage at Tanhuai and cut off urgent dispatches between Fen and Jin, tears soaked his robe—how timid he was!
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he halted his carriage at Tanhuai and cut off urgent dispatches between Fen and Jin, tears soaked his robe. How timid he was!

sentences.zh: 是知時之來也，雕虎可以生風；

translations.literal: Thus one knows that when the times come, even a carved tiger can give birth to wind;
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows that when fortune arrives, even a carved tiger can give birth to wind;

sentences.zh: 運之去也，應龍不免為醢。

translations.literal: when fortune departs, even the responsive dragon cannot escape becoming mince.
translations.idiomatic: when fortune departs, even the responsive dragon cannot escape becoming mince.

sentences.zh: 則項籍悲歌於帳下，信不虛矣！

translations.literal: Then Xiang Yu's mournful song beneath his tent—truly it was no empty tale!
translations.idiomatic: Then Xiang Yu's mournful song beneath his tent. Truly it was no empty tale!
